A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research-framing study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including material shifted by pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original system evaluations, findings from its annotated collection of 49 hate-speech papers, and an automated analysis of 102 recent fact-checking papers.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and data analyses, including the main performance tables and appendix results.

M1.justification: The extraction, NLI clustering, logical ranking, and LLM classification pipeline is unchanged. Section 3 revises notation and explanatory wording; the operational rules in Appendix C and prompts in Appendix F remain the same.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same existing automated fact-checking dataset, the same 49-paper hate-speech collection, and the same 102 fact-checking papers from January 2023 through December 2024. No evaluated domain, task, or scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The LLM baseline, all-paragraph and oracle variants, human reference, and sample-count comparisons retain their participation in the corresponding experiments. The newly cited SWIF2T system is a writing-assistance analogy, not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The annotation procedure, validation/test settings, paragraph-selection conditions, Gemini model, sampling settings, thresholds, and fMRR, Jaccard, and F-score metrics remain unchanged. The new temporal qualification of underspecification does not revise the documented annotation instructions or evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Both retain the sample-count analysis in Appendix B.1, all-versus-oracle comparisons, confidence-tier retention analysis, and discussions of framing-specific errors and literature examples. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 4–5 report the same 95% confidence intervals over 15 runs in both versions. The annotation agreement reporting, including Krippendorff's alpha of 0.61, is also unchanged; no new statistical procedure or seed information is introduced.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 2–6 and the distributions in Figures 4–5 are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains system test Jaccard scores of 34.86 for AFC and 31.37 for HS, against baseline scores of 28.45 and 16.79. The reported literature trends and qualitative findings also remain the same.

T1.justification: Section 3 distinguishes element categories, candidate labels, and supporting label sets more explicitly, but retains equivalent likelihood, clustering, min/max aggregation, and confidence-tier mathematics. The Boolean mappings in Appendix C are unchanged, and no theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies its opening claim about aligning research with practical applications by adding 'when researchers claim that their findings have real-world impact.' This modestly narrows the stated motivation; the methodological contributions, comparative-performance claims, and principal literature-trend claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2 newly specifies that underspecification concerns clarity in the paper's contemporary context, rather than compliance with later community standards. The introduction also distinguishes research framing from political/media and semantic framing. The limitations retain their existing restrictions on peer-review use and add a SWIF2T analogy for writing assistance.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, annotation guidelines, logical mappings, and full prompts are retained. Both PDFs provide the same code-and-annotations repository link; no technical resource, access instruction, or reproducibility setting is added or removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Card et al. (2016) when distinguishing research framing from other framing concepts, and Chamoun et al. (2024) when relating writing assistance to SWIF2T. These are limited additions to the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 replaces many generic uses of 'vague' with 'underspecified,' renames the umbrella category 'Scientific inquiry' to 'Knowledge exploration,' clarifies Section 3 notation, expands introductory explanations, and adds acknowledgments. The overall section organization and nearly all appendix wording remain intact.

P2.justification: The five figures and seven tables are retained. Limited edits update category labels and captions, correct Table 5's caption from F1class to F1sys, and alter table placement and equation layout through reflow. The diagrams and distribution plots are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves interpretive precision through the abstract's impact qualification, Section 2's temporal boundary for underspecification, and clearer distinctions between element categories and labels in Section 3. The corrected Table 5 caption also improves consistency. These resolve limited ambiguities while preserving the same empirical evidence and substantive limitations.
